topics.label: Introduction to Cancer Biology and Course Overview
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture series, outlines key learning outcomes, and frames the clinical and biological significance of cancer.

topics.label: Cellular Foundations and Developmental Basis of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: They describe how cancer arises from accumulated genetic changes and the breakdown of normal tissue differentiation programs, along with experimental approaches to study these cells.

topics.label: Tumor Invasion, Stepwise Progression, and Classification
topics.groupedBecause: They explore the histological criteria separating benign from malignant tumors through tissue invasion, metastatic pathways, stepwise progression models, and standard nomenclature.

topics.label: Pathophysiological Mechanisms of Cancer Morbidity and Mortality
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the physiological, structural, and systemic mechanisms through which primary and metastatic tumors impair normal tissue function and cause patient death.

topics.label: Patterns of Cancer Incidence in Humans and Other Species
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the epidemiology of cancer across various human tissue lineages as well as comparative incidence patterns across diverse animal taxa.

topics.label: Principles and Applications of Clinical Cancer Screening
topics.groupedBecause: They evaluate the rationale, clinical benefits, and organ-specific limitations of screening protocols designed to detect precursor and malignant lesions.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Practical Preview
topics.groupedBecause: It summarizes the session, directs students to review learning outcomes, and provides housekeeping for upcoming practicals.
